text:
They want the phone to read the text on the screen out loud, because on a foggy monday their eyes feel tired.
Read this out loud.
Can you read my screen to me?
Speak the words on this page, please.
My eyes hurt. Could you read this article for me?
Read it to me. No, wait, just the first paragraph.
Please raise the volume and read my messages aloud.
Read the text on this page slowly. Actually, make that the whole page, not just the top.
Would you be so kind as to read my emails aloud? I left my glasses at home.

Odile came home after a night shift, tired and hungry. She tied her belt over her robe and looked at her daily soup recipe on the phone. It made six bowls, but only she and her sister would eat. "Cut this recipe in half," Odile said. The assistant changed six bowls to three and read out the new list: one carrot, half an onion and two cups of broth. Odile asked for the steps. The assistant said, "Stir the pot every few minutes." "Remind me to stir in five minutes," said Odile. "I might fall asleep." The assistant set a timer for five minutes. When it rang, Odile stirred the soup and smiled.

They want a few gift ideas for a friend who hates the cold and loves coffee.
Gift ideas for my friend, please.
What should I get my mum for her birthday? Nothing too expensive.
Any ideas for a present under twenty dollars?
I need something for a friend who feels cold all the time. Not a scarf, she has plenty.
Help, the party is tomorrow and I have no present.
Suggest two or three birthday gifts for my brother, cheaper than a drip coffee maker.
Could you think of a gift that costs half as much as last year's?
I'm looking for a thoughtful present for my teacher. Could you give me a few ideas?

Person: Can you book someone to fix our kitchen tap?
Assistant: Yes. What day would you like them to come?
Person: Mum was cutting a raw onion and the tap dripped on her. Tomorrow, please.
Assistant: Tomorrow, got it. Morning or afternoon?
Person: Morning. No, wait, afternoon. I have school in the morning, and I love to watch the repair man.
Assistant: Afternoon, then. Is two o'clock okay?
Person: Yes, two is good.
Assistant: Done. A plumber will come tomorrow at two o'clock.

Kai stood in the office bathroom and looked in the mirror. "My hair is so long I can hardly see," Kai said to the phone. The assistant understood that Kai needed a haircut. It found a barber near the office with a free slot at half past five and asked, "Should I book it?" "Yes, please," said Kai. The assistant booked the haircut and said the barber was a ten minute ride away by bicycle. Kai did not want to miss it, so the assistant set a reminder for five o'clock. Kai finished the whole afternoon report without worrying, and left the office on time with the bicycle helmet in hand.

They want to book a dentist visit that is not far from home, in a block of free time.
Book a dentist, please.
I need a dentist this week.
Find a dentist that is not far from my house and book the first slot.
Check when the dentist opens and book me in for Friday.
Can you fill my free block on Thursday with a dentist visit and send me a reminder?
My tooth hurts, so get me in today, and tell me how far the clinic is.
I'd be grateful if you could look up dentists close to work and book one for next Monday morning.
Please see if Dr. Lee has a gap on Tuesday, and if not, try Wednesday.

Email is a way to send a message to someone far away in a few seconds. The inbox is where new mail lands. People change how it works all the time. They say "Show only unread mail" or "Put the newest message first." When you write an email, you can add a file, like a photo or a bill, by saying "Attach the picture to this email." Be careful with the send button. If someone sends too soon, they say "Undo that email" or "Wait, don't send it yet." To answer someone, you can say "Reply to Tom and tell him I'll be late." Some people also ask to mute a long chat so it stops buzzing.

Babak had just moved to the city and found running shoes at the back of the closet. "Plan a five kilometre run near here," Babak told the phone. The assistant showed a loop around the lake with a maximum climb of forty metres. Babak thought for a moment. "Sorry, make it three kilometres. It has been months, and I want to skip the hills." The assistant changed the plan to a flat three kilometre loop along the river and said the start was an eight minute walk from the flat. "Want me to count your steps?" it asked. "Yes, please," said Babak. The assistant started tracking and wished Babak a good first run.

They want the pet feeder to give the dog dinner now, one scoop of dry food, the kind with no corn.
Feed the dog.
It's time for Max's dinner.
I want him to have a scoop of dry food, the one without corn.
Give Luna one scoop of dry food. Actually, make it two.
Has the dog eaten? If not, open the feeder.
Drop the evening meal, but only half the usual. He's getting chubby.
Could you please serve the dry food at six? Sorry, I meant half past six.
Please start the feeder. I forgot to feed her before I left.

Keoni was parked outside a bakery, waiting for a passenger. "Read my notifications, but not the ads," Keoni said to the phone. The assistant read out two messages. A woman named Rosa had posted a photo of a sweet cake and invited everyone to join her baking group. "Don't join the group," said Keoni. "I have no time for it. Just like her post." The assistant liked the post and left the invite alone. Then it said, "You have no new followers today." Keoni laughed. The passenger waved from the door of the bakery, and the phone went quiet.

Dana was packing lunches when the laptop screen began to flash. With one hand, Dana typed fast: "why is my scren flashing and the internet slow". The assistant read it as a question about the screen and the internet. It turned off battery saver, which makes some screens flicker, and restarted the wifi. "Done," it said. "The flashing should stop, and the internet should be back in a minute." Dana looked up from the sandwiches. The screen was fine again, and the page loaded fast. "Thanks," Dana typed, "you saved my morning." Then Dana grabbed two lunch boxes and ran out to catch the school bus.

An appointment saves a time for you, like a haircut or a visit to the dentist. The shop or clinic keeps a calendar, and you pick a slot. People change appointments often. They say "Move it to Friday," "Make it later" or "Cancel my haircut." They also ask what time a place opens or closes. If a waiting room is loud and busy, someone might ask for the first slot of the morning. A person wearing a new skirt to a party may book a hair appointment right before it. Please don't skip a booking without telling the shop. Say "I can't come, cancel it," so someone else can have the time.

Cars need small checks to stay safe. Tyre pressure matters, because too little air wears tyres down, so people ask "How much air is in my tyres?" Fuel is what makes the engine go, and people ask "How much petrol is left?" On cold mornings some drivers warm up the car and say "Start the engine ten minutes before I leave." Others forget where they parked and ask "Where is my car?" For some people, fixing and washing a car is a hobby. If the dashboard shows a strange light, you can scroll through the car's menu or ask "What does this light mean?" Small questions like these keep the car happy.

name: set_subtitles
does: Turns subtitles on or off for the show that is playing, so people can follow it when the sound is weak or the actors mumble, and keeps them on until the show is finished.
inputs: on or off, the language, and how long to keep them, such as a stretch of ten minutes or the whole show
people say:
- I can't hear what they're saying
- Put the words on the screen
- Turn on captions, please
- Spanish subtitles, please
- The actors are whispering, can you show the text?
- Hide the writing at the bottom now

Person: Hello. I'm buying new seeds for the north side of my garden, and I need to work out the price. Could you please help me? My glasses are in the shed, and the numbers on the shop sign are too small.
Assistant: Of course. What are the numbers?
Person: The seeds cost twelve dollars a packet and I want five packets. There is a discount too.
Assistant: How much is the discount? A percentage, or a number of dollars?
Person: Ten percent off.
Assistant: Five packets cost sixty dollars. With ten percent off, you pay fifty-four dollars.
Person: Wonderful. Could you also iron my work shirt while I shop?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't iron shirts. I can only help with numbers and questions.
Person: Ha, fair enough. I'll do it myself.

Isaac wanted to book a table for six on Friday evening. "Find a restaurant near the office, but not a loud one, and no pizza," Isaac told the phone. One of the guests would bring a child, so a quiet place with a children's menu was best. The assistant sorted the nearby places by distance and took out the pizza places. It found a small restaurant called Lotus Garden and asked, "Is seven o'clock the exact time you want?" "Yes," said Isaac. The assistant booked a table for six at seven, and sent the address to Isaac's phone.

Minh wanted to be strong like the cyclists on TV, but the gym was closed and the bike had a flat wheel. So Minh asked the speaker at home, "Show me an easy workout for after school, at half past four." The assistant set an alarm for four thirty and said it would sound like a bell. When the bell rang, the assistant said, "Do ten jumping jacks, ten squats and ten push-ups on your knees. Rest for one minute between sets." Minh did the workout on the living room floor, and the assistant counted each set out loud. At the end it said, "Great job. Tomorrow is a rest day."

Drinks come in many strengths. Tea can be weak or strong, coffee can be light or dark, and a smoothie can be thick or thin. People ask for changes all the time: "Make it sweeter," "Less sugar, please," "No ice" or "A bit stronger." On a pizza night, a family may ask for a big bottle of lemonade. When a cup is empty, someone says "Fill it up" or "One more, please." If you are not at the cafe, you can ask the assistant to forward your usual order to the shop, like "Send my coffee order to the cafe on Main Street." Then it is ready when you arrive.

Sakura sat at the dinner table with a fork in hand while soup began to heat on the stove. The ceiling light was too bright. "Excuse me," Sakura said to the speaker, "would you mind making the ceiling light softer and a little warmer? My eyes get tired in the evening, and I would like to read my book at the table." The assistant lowered the light to thirty percent and changed the colour to a warm yellow. Sakura looked at the black window, where the room now shone gently, and said, "Lovely. Thank you." The assistant said, "You're welcome. Enjoy your book."

name: speak_screen_text
does: Reads the words on the screen out loud and stays true to the text, so people can choose to listen instead of read.
inputs: what to read, such as the whole page, one paragraph or a recipe for soup, and how fast to read it
people say:
- Can you read this to me?
- I can't see the small print
- Say what's written on this page
- Read the recipe slowly, my eyes are tired
- Just the second paragraph, please

Somchai held a newspaper in one hand and the phone in the other. The washing machine had stopped, and a red light kept blinking. "Please fix this blinking light and tell me how to wash the towels," Somchai said. Somchai was not good with technology, so the assistant spoke slowly. "The light means the door is not closed. Push the door until it clicks." Somchai pushed, and the light went off. "For the towels," the assistant said, "choose the double rinse and turn the dial to forty degrees." Somchai turned the dial and pressed start. The machine began to hum, and Somchai went back to the newspaper.

Errands are small trips to get things done, like going to the post office or the bank. Many errands have a deadline. If a gift must arrive by Friday, you have to ship it by Wednesday, so people say "Send this parcel by Thursday" or "When does the post office close?" If the bank is far away, they ask "Which branch is closest?" Some people like to put their errands in order and say "Remind me to pick up my package before five." Once an errand is done, they say "Cross it off my list" and put the receipt away.

A meeting is a time when people talk about work together, in a room or on a call. To join a call, people click a link or say "Join my ten o'clock meeting." During the call they say "Share my screen" or "Mute me for a moment." An agenda is a short list of topics, and people say "Show me the agenda" or "Let's sweep through it quickly." When the calendar is full, someone might ask "Find a free slot on Thursday" or "Move this meeting to the afternoon." Many people also keep a pen and paper nearby, and ask the assistant, "Write down what we decided."

Rachel closed the shop for lunch while an audiobook played from the speaker. "Pause the book," Rachel said. "Find a place nearby where I can get a table for two at half past twelve." The shop was in a temporary hut while workers build the new front, so Rachel did not want to walk far. The assistant found a noodle restaurant two streets away and said, "They have a table for two. It is a twelve minute walk." "Book it," said Rachel. The assistant booked the table and set a reminder for twenty minutes before. Then it said, "I will start the audiobook again when you sit down."

name: which_bin
does: Tells people which bin an item goes in and when that bin is collected, which is great for sorting rubbish at home, and can repeat the reminder every week.
inputs: the item, such as a coffee filter, a bottle or a banana peel, and the street where the person lives
people say:
- Where does this coffee filter go?
- Is a pizza box recycling?
- Which bin goes out tomorrow?
- Do the cans go in the blue one?
- Can this go in the compost?

name: read_recipe_steps
does: Reads the steps of a dish one at a time, in order, from a cookbook or from the person's own saved recipes.
inputs: the name of the dish, and whether it comes from a book or a personal collection
people say:
- What do I do next?
- Walk me through the lasagne
- Say that step again
- Read me grandma's cake recipe
- Which step am I on?
- Go back one step

name: next_departure
does: Tells people when the next bus or train leaves a stop, and whether the station has a toilet or sells tickets.
inputs: the stop or station, and the direction or final stop
people say:
- When is the next bus to the airport?
- How long until the train leaves?
- Is the number nine running late?
- Can I get a ticket at this station?
- Is there a toilet at the station?
- When does the next one come?

Sabine stood at a sunny bus stop with a cough, hoping to stop at the pharmacy on the way home. "Bus tracker," Sabine said to the phone. The assistant began to track bus fourteen and said, "It will arrive in four minutes." Sabine nodded and said, "Pharmacy hours?" The assistant answered, "The pharmacy on Oak Street is open until seven tonight. It is two stops from here." "Thanks," said Sabine. When the bus came, the assistant said, "Your bus is here." Sabine got on, found a seat by the window and leaned back in the sunshine.

They speak into the phone's microphone and want the robot mower to cut the grass before friends arrive.
Mow the lawn.
Start the robot mower.
Cut the grass before my friends come. I invited six people for Saturday.
Can the mower go out at two? Actually, make that three. The kids are still playing.
The lawn is a jungle, please do something.
I'd like the grass short enough for guests to sit comfortably, so please run the mower this morning.
Send the mower out, but skip the edges by the flower bed.
Please start the mowing now. Oh, wait, not the back garden, only the front.

Person: hey whats 18 times
Assistant: 18 times what number?
Person: 4. its for parking, 4 hours at 18 each. dont do the tax thing
Assistant: Okay, no tax. Four hours at 18 each is 72.
Person: ok thx. now halve it, my friend pays half
Assistant: Half of 72 is 36.
Person: also can u drink my pink smoothie and tell me if its good lol
Assistant: Sorry, I can't drink anything. But I hope it's tasty!

Time management means using your day well. A messy day can feel long, so people add small routines: a morning routine with toast and butter, a short walk after lunch, a quiet hour at night. A focus timer helps people work without stopping. They say "Set a timer for twenty-five minutes" or "Start a focus session." Breaks matter too, so they say "Remind me to rest in an hour" or "Make my break ten minutes." A good routine can win back time you would lose to scrolling. People also say "Move my break later" when work runs long.

name: wake_up_call
does: Sets a gentle morning alarm and can swap the wake time of one day for another, so people sleep well and wake up rested.
inputs: the day, the time, and a sound, such as birdsong or rain falling on a plant
people say:
- Wake me at six tomorrow
- Gentle alarm, please
- I want to sleep in on Saturday
- Make my alarm later today, I was up late
- Swap tomorrow's alarm with Sunday's
- Birds in the morning instead of the beep

Bram was flying on Saturday, and the plane left early in the morning. "Move my doctor visit to Thursday," Bram told the phone. The assistant checked the calendar and said, "You already have a haircut on Thursday at three." "Then compare my free days this week," said Bram. The assistant listed Wednesday morning and Friday afternoon. Bram looked outside at the raw, cold weather and said, "Wait, not Thursday. Put it on Friday, in the afternoon." The assistant moved the visit to Friday at two o'clock and added a reminder for one hour before. "Good," said Bram. "Now I can pack in peace."

They want the living room blinds, the ones with the label Sun Room in the app, opened to let light in.
Open the blinds.
It's so dark in here.
I can't see a thing in this room.
It's too gloomy. I can't find the toy my kid dropped.
The plants need some light.
Could the room get some daylight?
Pull up the shades, please.
Would you please let some daylight into the living room? It is hard to read.
Lift them straight up to the top.

Person: It's freezing in here. I just put my suitcase down.
Assistant: I can warm it up. Which room are you in?
Person: The bedroom. The kitchen is fine. I cooked dinner there.
Assistant: What temperature would you like in the bedroom?
Person: Around twenty. The window is wet, too. I wiped it twice.
Assistant: Done. The bedroom heating is set to twenty degrees, and it will take about twenty minutes. I can't wipe the window for you, but a warm room will help it dry.
Person: Thanks, that is kind.

Jasmine had a fancy new smart speaker on the shelf but did not know what to do with it. The day at the job had been long, and the evening seemed to drag. "It's so quiet in here," Jasmine said. The speaker answered, "Would you like some music?" "Oh, yes," said Jasmine. "Something soft." The speaker played gentle piano music at a low volume. Jasmine said, "A little louder." The speaker turned the volume up by two steps. Jasmine sat down on the sofa and smiled. "This is nice," Jasmine said. "Maybe technology is not so hard."

Ximena had just moved to the city and had spent the whole afternoon mopping the floors of the new flat. There was no food in the kitchen. "Excuse me," Ximena said to the phone, "could you please find a restaurant nearby that delivers? I just moved here, I'm tired from mopping, and I haven't found the grocery store yet. Something cheap, please, because I will be eating out daily this week." The assistant found a small Thai place with a lunch deal that would shave three dollars off the price. "Shall I order the pad thai?" it asked. "Yes, please," said Ximena, and sat down to wait.

name: link_rooms
does: Plays the same music on several speakers at once, so sound fills the house without leaking into rooms where people want quiet.
inputs: which rooms to include, such as the kitchen or the north bedroom, what to play, and a day if it repeats, like every tuesday
people say:
- Play the same song everywhere
- Music in the kitchen and the living room
- Put the news on in every room except the baby's
- Make all the speakers play together
- Turn the garden speaker on too

They want the score of the football match while they chill on the sofa.
Score?
What's the score in the match?
Is my team winning?
Who's ahead right now?
The dinner is cooked and I'm eating carrots in front of the TV. How is the game going?
Tell me the score every twenty-five minutes.
I'm just chilling. Can you update me on the Lions match?
Could you please tell me how the Lions are doing? They were two goals down at half time.

name: send_text_message
does: Writes a text to one person or a group and reads it back so the person can double check it before it goes out.
inputs: who gets the text, and what it should say
people say:
- Tell Sam the washer is broken
- Text Jo, I hope the knee heals fast
- Message the family group that dinner is at seven
- Let Mum know I'm running late
- Reply yes to Priya

Lights make a room useful. A lamp by the bed is good for reading, and a ceiling light is good for cooking. In a museum the lights are low so the old paintings stay safe. At home, people change their lights all day. They say "Dim the lamp," "Make it brighter" or "Turn off the hall light." With smart bulbs they can also change the colour, like "Make it warmer" or "Blue, please." A clear white light is good for work, and a soft yellow light is nice at night. If a room feels too sharp, people just say, "It's a bit much in here."

Seren was cooking lunch when the phone buzzed. The pet camera had spotted something strange. "Show camera," Seren said. The assistant showed the living room. The dog had climbed onto the seat of the sofa and was holding a shoe in its mouth. Seren laughed. "Text Ben," Seren said. The assistant asked, "What should I say?" "The dog has a shoe. Please come home and fetch it." The assistant sent the text and read it back. Ben replied after a minute: "On my way." Seren stirred the pot and kept watching the dog, who now looked very proud.

Food delivery brings a meal to your door. You pick a restaurant, choose a dish and say where to send it. A driver collects the food and may cross a river or a busy road on the way. When it rains, the trip can take longer, so people ask "How long until my food comes?" They also change small things: "Add extra sauce," "Leave it at the door" or "Ring the bell." At the end, many people add a tip, and say "Tip the driver two dollars" when the driver was polite and quick. If the food is late, they say "Where is my order?"

Person: Can you turn the pool pump on?
Assistant: Yes. For how long?
Person: Four hours. No, make it six. It rained all night and the water isn't clear.
Assistant: Six hours, okay. Should I run it now or later?
Person: Now, please. The kids are at school.
Assistant: Done. The pump is running and will stop at four this afternoon. I can't add salt to the pool myself. Would you like a reminder?
Person: Yes, remind me after school pickup.
Assistant: I will remind you at half past three.

Haruto's shop was closing soon, and the street outside was getting dark. "I have an idea," Haruto said to the phone. "Turn on the door camera and keep the recording twice as long as usual." The assistant switched on the camera and changed the recording from one week to two weeks. Haruto added, "Display the camera on the tablet at the counter." The assistant showed the front door on the tablet. "Do you want more motion alerts?" it asked. "No, fewer," said Haruto. "Only at night." The assistant set the alerts for night time only, and Haruto locked the door and went home.

name: keep_score
does: Keeps the score for each player in a game, so nobody has to count points on paper while they pass the salad around.
inputs: the players' names, their points, and how many rounds there are, so it can say when half are done
people say:
- Give Ana three points
- Who's winning?
- We're on round four now, mark it
- Zoe just got ten, write it down
- How many points does Dad have?
- Start the score fresh

The front door is the way into your home, and a lock keeps it safe. Some people use keys, and others use a code or a phone. People ask "Lock the front door," "Is the garage door closed?" or "Who is at the door?" A doorbell camera shows the person outside, and a yellow lamp by the door can light up when someone comes home. If a friend is visiting, you can say "Let Maria in" or "Open the door for a few minutes." Kids in a family often win the race to the door when the dog barks, and that is when people say "Check the camera."

A recipe usually tells you how much food to make for a number of people, like four. When more guests come, you can scale it. People say "Make it for six," "Half this recipe" or "Double the pancakes." Cups and spoons help with the amounts, and people ask "How many grams is a cup of flour?" A man who cooks for a big family may ask for a bigger batch every Sunday. If the dough is too loose, someone may ask "How much more flour do I need?" Many cooks also say "Draw up a shopping list for this recipe" so nothing is missing.

Arithmetic is working with numbers: putting them together, taking some away, making groups or sharing them out. People do it when they shop, split a bill or cook. They use a computer or a phone for it, and they say things like "Twenty plus ten," "Take five away from thirty," "Twice eight" or "Split twelve between three." Be careful with bills and tips, because one wrong number can change the total. If a cool drink costs three dollars and you want four, you might ask "What is three times four?" The answer, twelve, helps you decide how much money to bring.

Person: I need a room in Prague for the weekend, but not a hostel.
Assistant: Sure. Which nights, and how many guests?
Person: Friday and Saturday, just me. The news said it will freeze, so no place without heating.
Assistant: Got it. Do you want to stay in the centre?
Person: Close to it, but not too expensive. My recent trip cost too much.
Assistant: I found a small hotel with heating, near the centre, for eighty dollars a night. Shall I book it?
Person: Don't book yet. Just save it for me.
Assistant: Okay, I have saved it. Tell me when you want to book.
